description: Lambda-side Gateway exposure: the mandatory Gateway->Router adapter, the single-source-of-truth tool-schema registry, the ported assignee resolver, the three server-side composites, the four handler dispatch branches, and the Lambda-side unit + parity tests. This is the foundation both other features depend on (the agent's MCP mode talks to these Lambdas; the CDK stack reads tool_schemas.py). Independent of FEAT-002's agent code except that both consume tool_schemas.py / the strip invariant. Grounded in investigation section 3 (flat Gateway event, name on context.client_context.custom) and design sections 3-5.
steps: Create tools-lambdas/common/assignee.py: pure `resolve_assignee(assignee, developers) -> str|None` reproducing ALL SIX branches of agent/tools/jira_tools.py::_resolve_assignee EXACTLY (empty->None; `dev-` prefix passthrough returning the lowercased value WITHOUT consulting developers; exact full-name or email match; first-name/partial/email-local-part single match; ambiguous len(matches)!=1 ->None). Stdlib only; no HTTP.

Create tools-lambdas/common/tool_schemas.py: an authoritative registry of all 25 tools (19 read + 6 write), each a dict {name, description, inputSchema, method, path_template, arg_mapping, composite}. inputSchema is a JSON-Schema-subset object (top-level type 'object', properties, required) whose property names/types/required-ness EXACTLY match the current @tool signatures. Encode the design section 5.3 quirks verbatim: github_get_commits query `author` (NOT author_id); github_get_pull_requests query `status, author_id`; github_create_branch body {name:<branch_name>, from_branch} (route reads body['name']); jira_update_story PUT changed-fields-only with assignee name->dev-id; servicenow_list_deployments query `service, environment, status`; servicenow_list_incidents query `severity, status, service` (do NOT expose assignee); flag jira_search_stories, jira_get_stories_by_assignee, servicenow_deployment_status_by_project as composite=True with handler refs. Verify route verbs/paths against tools-lambdas/<svc>/routes.py.

Create tools-lambdas/jira/composites.py (search_stories, stories_by_assignee) and tools-lambdas/servicenow/composites.py (deployment_status): reproduce the agent-only orchestration server-side. Jira composites resolve assignee via common.assignee.resolve_assignee (using /developers), fan out over /projects -> /projects/{id}/stories through the in-Lambda router, apply the keyword filter (search only), return the same JSON records. ServiceNow deployment_status joins /services + /deployments and produces the grouped-by-service aggregation matching agent/tools/servicenow_tools.py::servicenow_deployment_status_by_project. Return plain JSON dicts, not formatted strings.

Create tools-lambdas/common/gateway_adapter.py with handle(tool_name, store, router, event)->dict: strip '___' prefix via rsplit('___',1)[-1]; look up the tool_schemas descriptor; if composite dispatch to the service composite and return its JSON; else fill path_template with path args, map remaining args to query (GET) or JSON body (POST/PUT) per arg_mapping, INJECT the expected X-API-Token (from the Lambda's MOCK_<SVC>_TOKEN env var) into a synthetic Function-URL-v2 event so the frozen require_token passes, call router.dispatch, then on statusCode in (200,201) return json.loads(result['body']) else return {'error': f"Request failed with status {status}: {result['body']}"} (byte-identical to agent/tools/http.py::make_request). Implement the design section 5.4 error table (unknown tool, missing required arg, 4xx/5xx, composite raise); never raise for an expected failure.

Modify all four tools-lambdas/<svc>/handler.py: INSIDE the existing try/except (ClientError->503, Exception->500) and AFTER store.ensure_seeded(), read the tool name via getattr(getattr(context,'client_context',None),'custom',None) -> custom.get('bedrockAgentCoreToolName'); if present return gateway_adapter.handle(tool_name, store, router, event); else fall through to the unchanged router.dispatch(event). Pass the freshly constructed store, router (never the stale _store global).

Create tools-lambdas/tests/test_gateway_adapter.py: synthetic Gateway events (flat args map + fake context.client_context.custom['bedrockAgentCoreToolName']) for a representative read, write, error (404/409) and composite per service; assert the dispatched route, the unwrapped JSON payload equals the route body data, and the error string equals make_request's for the same raw body. Use the moto/make_event fixtures from tests/conftest.py.

Create tools-lambdas/tests/test_tool_schemas.py: assert all 25 names present; the six write names equal WRITE_TOOL_NAMES; every schema top-level type=='object'; EXACT bidirectional arg-set equality between each DIRECT @tool signature (read via inspect.signature) and its schema properties keys; NO name in tool_schemas.py contains the substring '___'.

Create tools-lambdas/tests/test_composites_parity.py: one shared developer fixture fed to common.assignee.resolve_assignee asserting identical resolution across all six branches (exact-name, first-name, email-local-part, no-match, dev-3 passthrough against an empty fixture, ambiguous->None); and assert the ServiceNow composite grouped JSON matches the agent aggregation's data for the same services/deployments fixture.
acceptance_criteria: `cd tools-lambdas && python -m pytest tests -q` passes, including the new adapter, tool_schemas, and composite-parity tests AND the pre-existing handler tests (the HTTP/Function-URL path is unchanged).
tool_schemas.py contains exactly 25 descriptors; the six write names equal agent/approval.py WRITE_TOOL_NAMES; no name contains '___'.

A synthetic Gateway event for github_create_branch dispatches POST /repos/{repo_id}/branches with body key `name` and returns the route's JSON body on 201; a 409 returns the make_request-equivalent error string.
common.assignee.resolve_assignee is the single resolver body; the composites import it (no duplicate resolver).
